question.problem:
Emails arrive in a professor's inbox continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of $2$ emails per day. If the professor has not received an email for the past $3$ days, what is the probability that an email will arrive in the next $2$ days? Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**

The required probability is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Since emails arrive continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next email using the exponential distribution.

Let $X$ represent the time, in days, until the next email arrives. Given that emails arrive at an average rate of $2$ per day, the rate parameter is $\lambda =2$ emails per day, and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(2).
$$

Recall that exponential random variables have the memoryless property. Therefore, given two positive real numbers $s,t,$ we have that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

We can compute the complementary conditional probability as follows:

$$
P(X\le s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-{e}^{-\lambda t}
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =2,$ $s=3,$ and $t=2.$ 

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3+2\,|\,X>3) & =P(X\le 2) \\  & =1-{e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & =1-{e}^{-(2)(2)} \\  & =1-{e}^{-4} \\  & ≈0.982.\end{aligned}
$$
